title: Periodic Table 3D Interactive Explorer with Physics Debug Overlay
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js (via CDN) that implements a fully interactive 3D Periodic Table Explorer with a physics debug overlay.

## Scene Setup
- Black background, perspective camera at position (0, 0, 80), FOV 60.
- Ambient light (0xffffff, 0.4) and a directional light (0xffffff, 0.8) at (10, 20, 15).
- Render at least the first 54 elements (H through Xe) of the periodic table.
- Each element is a 3D box (BoxGeometry 2.4 x 2.8 x 1.2) positioned in the standard periodic table grid layout (18 columns, rows as per standard table). Spacing: 3.0 units horizontally, 3.5 units vertically. Center the grid around origin.
- Color each element box by its category: alkali metals (#FF6666), alkaline earth (#FFDEAD), transition metals (#FFC0C0), post-transition (#CCCCCC), metalloids (#CC9966), nonmetals (#A0FFA0), halogens (#FFFF99), noble gases (#C0FFFF), lanthanides (#FFB0FF). Store the category string on each mesh userData.
- Each box front face displays: atomic number (top), symbol (center, large), element name (bottom) using canvas textures mapped to the front face.

## Element Data
- Store an array of element objects with fields: atomicNumber, symbol, name, atomicMass, category, group, period, electronegativity (Pauling scale, 0 if unknown), meltingPoint (K, 0 if unknown), boilingPoint (K, 0 if unknown).
- At minimum include accurate data for elements 1-54.

## Selection & Detail Panel
- Raycasting on click: clicking an element box selects it. The selected element gets a bright emissive outline (yellow emissive, 0.5 intensity). Previous selection is deselected.
- A DOM detail panel (div#detailPanel, positioned top-right, 280px wide) shows: symbol, name, atomic number, atomic mass, category, electronegativity, melting point, boiling point. Hidden when nothing is selected.
- Pressing Escape deselects the current element and hides the panel.

## Category Filter
- A DOM dropdown (select#categoryFilter) with options: 'all', 'alkali', 'alkaline_earth', 'transition', 'post_transition', 'metalloid', 'nonmetal', 'halogen', 'noble_gas', 'lanthanide'.
- When a category is selected, elements NOT in that category become semi-transparent (opacity 0.15) and non-interactive. 'all' restores everything.
- Filtering preserves the current selection if the selected element matches the filter; otherwise deselects.

## 3D Orbital View Mode
- A button (button#orbitalToggle, text 'Orbital View') toggles orbital view mode.
- When activated on a selected element, the element box animates (over 1 second) to screen center and scales up 3x. Electron shell rings (TorusGeometry) appear around it — one ring per electron shell (period number determines shell count, e.g., Na has 3 shells). Rings have radii 3, 5, 7, 9... and rotate at different speeds.
- Small spheres (radius 0.15, blue) orbit on each ring representing electrons. Distribute electrons per shell using simplified rule: 2, 8, 18, 18, 8 max per shell.
- Pressing 'Orbital View' again or pressing Escape exits orbital mode, animating back.

## Physics Debug Overlay
- A checkbox (input#debugOverlay, label 'Debug Overlay') toggles a physics debug HUD.
- When enabled, render a semi-transparent overlay (canvas or DOM, id='debugCanvas') showing:
  - FPS counter updated every frame
  - Camera position (x, y, z) rounded to 2 decimals
  - Number of visible elements
  - Number of draw calls (from renderer.info.render.calls)
  - If orbital mode is active: total electron count, average orbital angular velocity
- Update debug info every frame.

## Camera Controls
- OrbitControls for mouse rotation/zoom/pan.
- Keyboard: pressing 'R' resets camera to initial position (0,0,80) and target (0,0,0) with a smooth 0.5s tween.
- Keyboard: Arrow keys (Left/Right) cycle selection through elements by atomic number. Up/Down changes the current period row.

## Search
- An input field (input#searchBox, placeholder 'Search element...') filters elements by name or symbol as user types. Non-matching elements become transparent (opacity 0.1). Empty search restores all. Search interacts with category filter (both filters apply simultaneously).

## Undo/Redo Selection History
- Maintain a selection history stack. Each selection (by click or arrow key) pushes to history.
- Ctrl+Z undoes last selection (reverts to previous). Ctrl+Y redoes.
- History stack max depth: 50.

## Temperature Visualization Mode
- A button (button#tempMode, text 'Temp Mode') toggles temperature visualization.
- When active, each element box color interpolates from blue (lowest melting point) to red (highest melting point) across all elements. Elements with meltingPoint=0 show gray.
- A gradient legend bar (div#tempLegend) appears at the bottom showing the scale.

## State Management
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
  - selectedElement: {atomicNumber, symbol, name, category} or null
  - filterCategory: string ('all' or category name)
  - orbitalMode: boolean
  - orbitalShells: number (0 if not in orbital mode)
  - orbitalElectronCount: number (0 if not in orbital mode)
  - debugOverlayActive: boolean
  - debugFPS: number
  - debugDrawCalls: number
  - visibleElementCount: number (elements with opacity > 0.5)
  - cameraPosition: {x, y, z} (rounded to 2 decimals)
  - tempModeActive: boolean
  - searchQuery: string
  - selectionHistoryLength: number
  - selectionHistoryIndex: number (current position in history, -1 if empty)
  - totalElements: number (total element meshes created)
  - elementPositions: array of {atomicNumber, x, y, z} for first 10 elements
  - frameCount: number (incremented each frame)
  - lastInteraction: string ('none','click','keyboard','filter','search','orbital','debug','temp','undo','redo','reset')
physics_constraints: Electron orbital angular velocities must remain constant per shell (no drift). Camera reset must reach exact target position within epsilon 0.05. Element grid positions must be deterministic and reproducible. Filter and search transparency changes must be reversible to original state. Selection history must maintain strict stack ordering. Temperature color mapping must be monotonically increasing from blue to red. All numerical state values must be NaN-free at all times.
